source.title: Parameter Prediction for Unseen Deep Architectures
source.authors: Boris Knyazev; Michal Drozdzal; Graham W. Taylor; Adriana Romero-Soriano

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares training curves from two initializations on ResNet-50, reporting how initialization affects early learning speed. It does not test the other claim versions’ training-error outcomes.
record.gate_note: The SGD comparisons in Tables 3–4 report test accuracy, not training classification error, so they do not establish whether training reaches near-zero training error. The convergence-speed metric uses thresholds of 95% CIFAR-10 training top-1 accuracy and 10% ImageNet training top-5 accuracy, not near-zero error; no outcome for that metric is reported in the supplied text. The GHN-versus-He initialization training curves in Figure 13 bear on V4’s general initialization-speed topic.
record.test_reason: The study uses He-style scaling to normalize hypernetwork predictions and evaluates its parameter-prediction method. Its initialization comparison uses learned parameters in ResNet-50 and measures validation accuracy; it does not test V4's activation-matched initialization claim for plain networks, or any other specified version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. GHN-2 rapidly predicts useful parameters for diverse unseen architectures, but performance remains below conventional optimization. Its parameters benefit low-data transfer learning; on full-data CIFAR-10 ResNet-50, the early validation-accuracy advantage disappears when He initialization overtakes it after around five epochs.
record.recipe_differences: The paper’s main method predicts parameters with a hypernetwork rather than training the target network from random initialization. Figure 13 separately compares CIFAR-10 ResNet-50 training from GHN-predicted and He initializations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ResNet-50 initialization comparison changes over training time: GHN-2 initialization helps in the first few epochs, while He initialization outperforms it after around 5 epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 13 reports that GHN-2 initialization improves ResNet-50 validation accuracy during the first few CIFAR-10 training epochs, but He initialization overtakes it after around five epochs. Learning rate and weight decay are tuned separately for each initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned parameter initialization can improve early validation performance in residual networks without improving later performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Section B.2.2 and Figure 8 show that GHN-2's predicted ResNet-50 parameters initially produce activation variances resembling He initialization, whereas GHN-1's activations explode after hypernetwork training. This does not measure trainable depth or establish an initialization-driven training-speed effect in plain networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Operation-dependent scaling can stabilize activations when a hypernetwork predicts network parameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 6 reports better low-data CIFAR-10 test accuracy and Penn-Fudan detection performance after fine-tuning GHN-2 initializations than He initializations across three architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ImageNet-trained hypernetworks can supply useful initial parameters for low-data transfer learning.

record.problems: The relevant initialization comparison is presented as a figure without numerical values in the text; exact accuracy differences and uncertainty cannot be extracted. The study does not report near-zero training classification error for the SGD comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the SGD comparison tables report test accuracy rather than the claim’s training-error outcome. The convergence-speed property is defined using training-accuracy thresholds, but the supplied text does not report its measured values.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error from random initialization, including corrupted or random labels. Tables 3–4 report test accuracy; the convergence-speed thresholds do not establish near-zero training error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of adding student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth in plain networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.

Whether activation-matched initializations preserving signals and gradients accelerate learning or increase trainable depth in plain networks; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep orthogonal convolutions.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Controlled comparisons of gradient-training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 assignment broadens the version to any initialization-dependent learning curve. Figure 13 concerns a residual network and learned initialization, and its vertical axis is validation accuracy. No result rows were supplied, and no omitted result directly tests a specified version.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports test accuracy for SGD-trained networks but does not report whether training classification error reaches zero or near zero, including under random or corrupted labels.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or local-minimum outcomes.
The study does not compare plain and residual networks’ training error as depth changes. Its BN-free results concern parameter prediction and test accuracy, not the claimed training-error effect.

Figure 13 compares GHN-predicted and He initialization for ResNet-50 on CIFAR-10, but the result is presented only as a figure without recoverable numerical values. Orthogonal initialization and training plain networks at greater depth are not tested.
No learning-rate stability-threshold or curvature experiment.
The study does not test whether batch normalization speeds gradient training or enables higher learning rates, nor whether Fixup reproduces those effects.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
